findings.claim: New in 70199b59. 70199b59 changed the control branch at verify-learner-test.mjs line 68 to choose the no-runnable message whenever the control run has no failed and no passed assertion. That also catches a control run whose learner test file failed to load: Vitest's JSON report then has one test file with status failed and an error message but no assertion results, so 'failed' is false and 'passed' is 0. Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 70199b59, with the private overlay copied over the starter and my own learner tests written in scratch. I wrote a correct learner test that also throws at module level only when the imported default export is not the learner's own component, so it loads in the normal run and fails to load under the mutation config. The normal run showed 'Test Files 8 passed (8)' and 'Tests 8 passed (8)', and npm test then printed 'no runnable test was found in starter/src/service-form.test.jsx. The file may be missing or empty, or hold only todo or skipped tests' and exited 1. The file exists, is not empty and has just passed. Running the control directly gave numFailedTestSuites 1, numTotalTests 0 and the thrown message in testResults[0].message; a deleted file gives numTotalTestSuites 0 and an empty testResults, so the two cases can be told apart. With the c68e4995 verifier swapped into scratch, the same file got the unchanged-copy message, which was closer for this learner-made case. The more likely trigger is on the harness side: when I added a module-level throw to a scratch copy of task8-variant.jsx (restored afterwards, sha256 checked), a correct test got the same no-runnable message. A variant or plugin load failure on a platform that has never been run (Windows and Linux are unverified) would therefore tell a learner with a finished test that their file may be missing or empty, and Vitest's own error is never printed. The verdict stays exit 1 and no weak test can be accepted this way; only the diagnosis is wrong. A Vitest configuration crash is not affected: with an invalid variant the run wrote no JSON, and the existing 'could not read the test results' path, which prints Vitest's output, still applies.
findings.recommendation: Take the no-runnable branch only when no test file in the control report has status failed (or when the report has zero test suites), and otherwise report the load error, ideally with the failed file's message, as the 'could not read the test results' path already does with Vitest's output. Trialled in scratch on 70199b59: adding a per-run flag for any failed test file and requiring it to be false in the line-68 condition kept the deleted-file, todo-only and skip-only messages, gave the module-level load error the unchanged-copy message again, and still accepted my correct test with exit 0. Printing the suite message was not trialled. Add a module-level load error to the private adversarial controls. Low on its own; it does not justify a further correction loop unless Firstmate decides otherwise.

Touched by 70199b59 under decision react-forms-loop5-polish item (a). The no-runnable branch (line 68) now fires when the control run has no failed and no passed assertion, whatever Vitest's exit status. Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 70199b59, with the private overlay copied over the starter and my own learner tests written in scratch. With starter/src/service-form.test.jsx deleted, the normal run showed 'Test Files 7 passed (7)' and 'Tests 7 passed (7)', then npm test printed only 'no runnable test was found in starter/src/service-form.test.jsx. The file may be missing or empty, or hold only todo or skipped tests. Write the test described in task 8 there.' and exited 1. The unchanged-copy message no longer appears for the deleted file. Running the control directly on the deleted file gave exit 1 with a JSON report of 0 suites and 0 tests, which is why the exit status had to be ignored. A todo-only file and a skip-only file got the same message with exit 1. An empty file never reaches it: Vitest's 'No test suite found in file ...' fails the normal run first, so 'or empty' in the message is harmless but unreachable through this branch. Regressions checked: my correct test is still accepted (Task 8 line, exit 0); a blank-only test still gets the four completed-submission messages; a name-only test still gets only the team message; and a test that genuinely fails against the unchanged copy still gets the unchanged-copy message. The new condition does misclassify one case: a learner test file that fails to load under the mutation config (one failed suite with an error, zero assertions) now gets the no-runnable message instead. That is raised as sme-fcc-w1 and does not reopen this item, whose deleted-file case is fixed.

Touched by 70199b59 under decision react-forms-loop5-polish item (b), which authorized only the message, not the label-query change in task8-variant.jsx; that file is unchanged (sha256 d85eae98... matches loop 5). Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 70199b59, with the private overlay copied over the starter and my own learner tests written in scratch. A scratch copy of the solved form with the name field labelled by aria-labelledby pointing at a 'Service name' caption just outside the form passes the normal run ('Tests 8 passed (8)'), and my correct test then gets only the reworded message (line 93) with exit 1. The message no longer tells the learner to finish tasks 1-2; it says the labelled fields could not be found inside the submitted form and to keep each field's labelling text inside the <form> element. Moving the caption inside the form was accepted with exit 0, so the advice matches the cause (Testing Library resolves aria-labelledby within the query container). The wrong-advice part of the claim is resolved. Residual, accepted by the decision scope: a correct form with an outside caption still fails closed instead of being accepted, and the verdict for weak tests is unchanged (a blank-only test on that form still gets the message plus the three completed-submission misses). The message is learner-safe; it names only labels and the form element.
